newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, further losses possible.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, further losses possible.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Wednesday on a low turnover and in thin trade, and analysts said no recovery was yet in sight for the market, with possible further losses in some stocks.
Traders put the blame for the unfavourable trend on the constellation of political and economic factors.
Last week Croatian capital saw first popular protests in years, while president Franjo Tudjman was said to be seriously ill.
"But at least political developments started having an influence on economy and on the market," said Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage.
"I don't want to be pessimistic, but some stock prices could take a serious dive," he added.
Of five active issues, two rose, one fell and two were flat. Volume shrank to 761 shares from Friday's 3,386, while turnover was three times lower at 865,305 kuna.
Traders said only 13 transactions were made on 385 offers.
Of the only two gainers, hotelier Arenaturist was up 20 kuna to 150, with 60 shares changing hands.
The other gainer, Zagrebacka Banka, inched up five kuna to 1,005, but was the most actively traded issue with 355 shares changing hands.
Zelimorski said only the two fully listed issues, Zagrebacka and drugs firm Pliva were likely to remain more or less stable.
Pliva traded flat at 12,600 kuna on a meagre volume of 36 units. Its GDR's were down to $48.625 from $50 on Friday.
Hotelier Suncani Hvar was flat at 60 kuna, with 150 shares sold.
The only loser was food processor Podravka, edging down five kuna and selling 160 shares.
